Explain the architectural design and implementation details of LemGendary Environment Manager: Technical Whitepaper > 3. Hybrid Cloud & Registry Integration from PAPER_ENV_MANAGER.

According to `PAPER_ENV_MANAGER.md` (LemGendary Environment Manager: Technical Whitepaper > 3. Hybrid Cloud & Registry Integration):

Seamless execution between local development stations (Windows 11 with
DirectX/DirectML, CUDA, or ROCm) and cloud execution clusters (Kaggle Linux
environments, headless HPC nodes) demands resilient registry binding.

The system implements dynamic index routing based on probed hardware attributes.
The probe checks the backends in the order CUDA, ROCm, Apple MPS, DirectML and
CPU. On CUDA hosts the index depends on the NVIDIA driver major version $d$
(`select_cuda_torch_index()`); an unknown or unparseable driver version selects
`cu126`:

$$
\text{IndexURL}(H) = \begin{cases} \text{.../whl/cu134}, & \text{if }
H.\text{backend} = \text{CUDA} \land d \ge 610 \\ \text{.../whl/cu126}, &
\text{if } H.\text{backend} = \text{CUDA} \land 560 \le d < 610 \\
\text{.../whl/cu121}, & \text{if } H.\text{backend} = \text{CUDA} \land 535
\le d < 560 \\ \text{.../whl/cu118}, & \text{if } H.\text{backend} =
\text{CUDA} \land d < 535 \\ \text{.../whl/rocm6.0}, & \text{if }
H.\text{backend} = \text{ROCm} \\ \text{PyPI}, & \text{if } H.\text{backend} =
\text{MPS} \\ \text{.../whl/cpu}, & \text{otherwise (DirectML or CPU)}
\end{cases}
$$

where `.../whl/` stands for `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/` and PyPI for
`https://pypi.org/simple`.

Since v16.9.70 the central requirements files carry no fixed `--extra-index-url`
line: the installer passes the probed index, so CPU hosts and older drivers no
longer receive `cu134` wheels. Since v16.9.71 macOS on arm64 reports one `mps`
device (unified memory as VRAM), the DirectML probe reads the 64-bit adapter
memory size from the registry (adapters above 4 GB no longer report 4095 MB) and
skips basic, Hyper-V, remote and virtual display adapters, and `rocm-smi` output
is read as CSV. The pinned versions (`torch==2.15.0`, `torchvision==0.29.2`,
`torchaudio==2.11.1`) are the same on every backend; only the wheel build
differs.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_ENV_MANAGER.md` (LemGendary Environment Manager: Technical Whitepaper > 6. Synthesis Flow & Topology > 6.3 Desktop GUI State Aggregation & Multi-Sidecar Ecosystem Observability):

To minimize HTTP handshake overhead in desktop graphical clients, the
Environment Manager daemon exposes high-density aggregated endpoints:

- **Liveness (`/api/ping`)**: Constant-time `GET` and `HEAD` probe returning
  `status`, `service` and `version`.
- **State Aggregation (`/api/gui/state`)**: Packages system identity, hardware
  sensors, discovered repository trees, and active pipeline statuses into a
  single non-blocking payload, eliminating waterfall polling.
- **Ecosystem Sidecar Interoperability (`/api/gui/ecosystem`)**: Probes the
  `lemgendary-datasets` sidecar (port 8100) and the `lemgendary-training-suite`
  sidecar (port 8200) one after the other in the thread pool, each with a 1.5 s
  timeout, and reports their health next to the env manager itself (port 8000)
  for the `lemgendary-ai-studio-gui` status bar.
- **Service Control (`/api/services/{service_id}/start` and `/stop`)**: Starts
  and stops the sidecar daemons. In v16.9.67, process termination is hardened
  via a two-tier strategy: recording the background process PID to
  `server.pid` upon launch, and executing Windows netstat parsing that
  recognizes both explicit IP bindings (`127.0.0.1`, `0.0.0.0`, `[::]`) and
  listening wildcard tokens (`*:*`, `:0`) to terminate stubborn lingering
  processes reliably. Furthermore, test environments enforce isolation
  via `LEM_DISABLE_SIDECAR_AUTORUN=1`.
- **Governance & Maintenance Endpoints (`/api/hooks/install`, `/api/clean`)**:
  Provides programmatic endpoints for ecosystem-wide Git hook installation and
  recursive temporary cache/staging artifact purges with space recovery
  telemetry.
- **API Contract**: `openapi.json` is regenerated from the running app and
  includes `run-step`, `hooks/install`, `ping`, `update/status`, `shutdown` and
  `bug-report`, so Tauri Rust and TypeScript clients can be generated from it.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_ENV_MANAGER.md` (LemGendary Environment Manager: Technical Whitepaper > 1. Abstract):

The LemGendary Environment Manager (release `v16.9.86-STABLE`) is the
infrastructure layer of the LemGendary ecosystem: it probes hardware, provisions
and audits virtual environments, keeps dependency manifests aligned, validates
the workspace and serves this functionality to the LemGendary AI Studio GUI as a
local sidecar on port 8000. It addresses environmental drift, non-deterministic
wheel resolution and accelerator fragmentation through a seven-step pipeline
that couples device probing, one-way manifest synchronization with a downgrade
guard, reverse-dependency upgrade classification with a constraint-preserving
pip dry-run that fails closed, and real-time WebSocket telemetry. The pipeline
is non-destructive by default; a clean reinstall needs an explicit option. The
sidecar accepts browser requests only from AI Studio GUI origins, never returns
stored secrets, runs package updates as background jobs and packages bug reports
into a local ZIP archive for the operator's own mail client. Its
`ecosystem/ecosystem.json` is the single source of the ports, project list,
pipeline steps and identity that every project reads (Section 6.7).

To quantify the operational efficiency gains delivered by the unified
architecture, benchmark evaluations were conducted comparing the legacy

| Operational Metric | Legacy PowerShell | `lem-env` | Factor |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| Cross-Project Dependency Audit | 18,900 ms | 1,420 ms | $13.3\times$ |
| Manifest Consistency Sync | Manual | 45 ms | $400\times$ |

| Capability | Legacy PowerShell | `lem-env` `v16.9.60` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| Remote observability | Console only | REST + WebSocket telemetry |

| Node.js / npm | None | Audit, install, `npm outdated` upgrades |

How do I operate LemGendary Environment Manager: Technical Whitepaper > 6. Synthesis Flow & Topology > 6.2 Dual-Interface Telemetry Topology in the LemGendary AI Studio GUI?

Reference: `PAPER_ENV_MANAGER.md` (LemGendary Environment Manager: Technical Whitepaper > 6. Synthesis Flow & Topology > 6.2 Dual-Interface Telemetry Topology).

The control topology couples a headless CLI engine (`lem-env`) and a reactive
desktop GUI shell (`lemgendary-ai-studio-gui`) via an asynchronous non-blocking
event stream:

$$
T_{\text{telemetry}} = \mathcal{O}(1) \quad \text{amortized broadcast}
$$

Pipeline and update worker threads dispatch typed `PipelineEvent` messages to
connected WebSocket clients through `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe()`, which
bridges the worker threads to the server event loop without blocking the UI
during prolonged package compilation and bytecode verification. The FastAPI
`@asynccontextmanager` lifespan handler starts the ecosystem sidecars in the
thread pool on startup.

To eliminate unobservable blocking stalls during dependency installation, the
execution subsystem deploys unbuffered real-time streaming generators
(`stream_pip_with_recovery`, `stream_npm_install`,
`stream_install_requirements`) that yield subprocess output line-by-line using
`PYTHONUNBUFFERED="1"` and `--progress-bar on`. Streaming lines are parsed in
real time to extract wheel download metrics (transfer bandwidth, byte ratios,
and ETA countdowns), requirement progress ratios (`[k/N requirements]`), and
discrete stage milestones, broadcasting typed progress events
(`is_progress=True`) over the `/ws/log` WebSocket channel without terminal
stream saturation.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_ENV_MANAGER.md` (LemGendary Environment Manager: Technical Whitepaper > 6. Synthesis Flow & Topology > 6.5 Security Model):

The sidecar binds to `127.0.0.1` by default and shares one security contract
with the other two sidecars and the GUI:

- **Origin Guard** (`env_manager/security.py`): a request whose `Origin` header
  is not an AI Studio GUI origin (`tauri://localhost`, `http://tauri.localhost`,
  `https://tauri.localhost`, `http://localhost:1420`, `http://127.0.0.1:1420`)
  gets `403`, and WebSocket handshakes from a foreign origin are refused.
- **Client Header**: browser requests that use `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or
  `DELETE` must send `X-LemGendary-Client: ai-studio-gui`. The custom header
  forces a CORS preflight, which blocks cross-site form posts. Requests without
  an `Origin` (CLI, scripts, tests) are not affected.
- **Closed CORS**: the CORS policy lists the same origins, explicit methods and
  headers, and `allow_credentials=False` instead of `allow_origins=["*"]`.
- **Masked Secrets** (`env_manager/secrets_vault.py`): `GET /api/secrets`
  returns only `has_value` and a `value_hint` (last 4 characters, empty for
  values shorter than 8) and has no side effects. `POST /api/secrets` is
  write-only: an empty value keeps the stored one, a non-empty value replaces
  it. The vault file `.secrets.yaml` is written atomically with a backup. Kaggle
  credentials are propagated only to repositories that read them, without
  invented usernames, and the result is reported in `propagation` (`written`,
  `skipped`, `failed`). All secret files are ignored by git.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_FOREX_PREDICTOR.md` (Multi-Scale CNN-Transformer Forex & Commodity Predictor > 3. Shared Foundations > 3.2 Cross-Timeframe Multi-Head Attention Fusion):

Given $T$ active timeframes, each timeframe encoder yields a summary
representation $\mathbf{z}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}$. The timeframe
embeddings are stacked into matrix
$\mathbf{Z} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d_{\text{model}}}$. Cross-timeframe
multi-head attention computes dynamic relational weights between all temporal
horizons:

$$
\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{Z} \mathbf{W}_Q, \quad \mathbf{K} = \mathbf{Z}
\mathbf{W}_K, \quad \mathbf{V} = \mathbf{Z} \mathbf{W}_V
$$

$$
\text{Attention}(\mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V}) = \text{softmax}\left(
\frac{\mathbf{Q} \mathbf{K}^T}{\sqrt{d_k}} \right) \mathbf{V}
$$

$$
\mathbf{e}_{\text{fused}} = \text{Concat}\left(\text{head}_1, \dots,
\text{head}_h\right) \mathbf{W}_O + \mathbf{E}_{\text{pair}}(p)
$$

where $\mathbf{E}_{\text{pair}}(p) \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}$ is the
learned pair embedding representing currency-specific volatility dynamics.

#### Timeframe Dropout Regularizer ($p=0.15$)

To prevent the attention mechanism from over-relying on high-frequency noise
from any single temporal rung or suffering from co-adaptation across adjacent
horizons, the fusion block incorporates **Timeframe Dropout Regularization**.
During training when $T > 1$ timeframes are active, a stochastic masking vector
$\mathbf{m} \in \{0, 1\}^T$ is sampled with drop probability
$p_{\text{tf}} = 0.15$:

$$
m_j \sim \text{Bernoulli}(1 - p_{\text{tf}}), \quad j \in \{1, \dots, T\}
$$

To eliminate catastrophic information blackout where all timeframes are dropped
simultaneously, an unconditional fallback gate ensures at least one timeframe
remains active:

$$
\mathbf{m}^* = \begin{cases} \mathbf{m}, & \text{if } \sum_{j=1}^T m_j > 0 \\
\mathbf{e}_{j^*}, \quad j^* \sim \mathcal{U}(1, T), & \text{if } \sum_{j=1}^T
m_j = 0 \end{cases}
$$

The masked timeframe embedding matrix
$\tilde{\mathbf{Z}} = \mathbf{Z} \odot (\mathbf{m}^*
\mathbf{1}_{d_{\text{model}}}^T)$ is then supplied to the cross-timeframe
projection matrices
($\mathbf{Q} = \tilde{\mathbf{Z}} \mathbf{W}_Q, \mathbf{K} = \tilde{\mathbf{Z}}
\mathbf{W}_K, \mathbf{V} = \tilde{\mathbf{Z}} \mathbf{W}_V$). This forces each
temporal encoder to maintain standalone predictive utility while compelling the
attention fusion layer to learn robust inter-temporal representations.

The overarching strategy of the LemGendary ForexPredictor is to construct a
**Financial Foundation Model**. Financial markets are not isolated bubbles; they
are a deeply interconnected ecosystem. For instance, when global equities (e.g.,
US500, GER40) experience severe drawdowns, capital typically flows into
safe-haven assets (XAUUSD spikes, USDJPY drops). By exposing the neural network
to 16 diverse assets simultaneously during training, the model is forced to
learn these hidden macro-economic correlations. This Cross-Asset Regularization
prevents the model from overfitting to the micro-structure of a single currency
pair, yielding a vastly more intelligent and resilient core brain that
understands universal market dynamics.

The 16-symbol physical manifold (`LemGendizedForexUniverseLarge`, 2019–2026)
holds 26,818,700 rows (the training registry count of
`LemGendizedForexUniverse`) across G7 currency pairs, precious metals, crude
energy, and major equity indices:

$$
\mathcal{U}_{\text{universe}} = \mathcal{U}_{\text{core}} \cup \{ \text{USDCAD},
\text{USDCHF}, \text{AUDUSD}, \text{NZDUSD}, \text{EURJPY}, \text{GBPJPY},
\text{EURGBP}, \text{XAGUSD}, \text{USOIL}, \text{US500}, \text{NAS100},
\text{DE40} \}
$$

To resolve heterogeneous brokerage ticker nomenclatures across live MetaTrader 5
terminals, the ingestion engine implements bidirectional **Symbol Aliasing**
($\text{NAS100} \leftrightarrow \text{USTEC}$,
$\text{DE40} \leftrightarrow \text{GER40}$). Alternate symbols are dynamically
mapped to canonical embedding indices and pip scale configurations, preventing
missing tensor key errors during multi-broker deployment.

Explain the architectural design and implementation details of Multi-Scale CNN-Transformer Forex & Commodity Predictor > 3. Shared Foundations > 3.1 Causal Convolution & Temporal Invariance from PAPER_FOREX_PREDICTOR.

According to `PAPER_FOREX_PREDICTOR.md` (Multi-Scale CNN-Transformer Forex & Commodity Predictor > 3. Shared Foundations > 3.1 Causal Convolution & Temporal Invariance):

To strictly prevent future lookahead leakage, all convolutional operations
employ left-sided zero padding. The dilated causal Conv1D operator at time $t$
for dilation rate $d$ and kernel size $K$ is defined as:

$$
\mathbf{h}_t = \text{GELU}\left( \sum_{k=0}^{K-1} \mathbf{W}_k \cdot
\mathbf{x}_{t - d \cdot k} + \mathbf{b} \right)
$$

By cascading $M$ layers with exponentially increasing dilation $d = 2^m$ for
$m \in \{0, 1, \dots, M-1\}$, the receptive field expands exponentially without
downsampling:

$$
\text{RF} = 1 + \sum_{m=0}^{M-1} (K - 1) \cdot 2^m = 1 + (K - 1)(2^M - 1)
$$

```text
Input Sequence:   x[t-3]   x[t-2]   x[t-1]   x[t]
                    \        \        \       /
Layer 1 (d=1):     h1[t-2]  h1[t-1]  h1[t]
                      \        \      /
Layer 2 (d=2):        h2[t-1]  h2[t]
                         \     /
Output Embedding:         z[t] (Zero Future Information Flow)
```

The CausalConv1D blocks implement **Stochastic Depth** (drop-path
regularization), which randomly drops entire layers during training, forcing the
network to learn robust, noise-invariant temporal features and preventing
overfitting to market idiosyncrasies.

largest peak-to-trough fall of $E$ in percent of the peak. An epoch without
a directional prediction reports no win rate, profit factor, Sharpe,

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_FOUNDATION_MODELS_MASTER.md` (Generative & Multimodal Foundation Models > 2. Foundation Scaling Laws & Compute Budgets > 2.2 First-Principles VRAM Allocation & Hardware Governors):

Memory containment during large-scale foundation model training requires exact
accounting across static allocations, dynamic activations, and framework
overhead:

$$
M_{\text{total}} = M_{\text{params}} + M_{\text{grads}} + M_{\text{opt}} +
M_{\text{activations}} + M_{\text{workspace}}
$$

#### 1. Parameter Memory ($M_{\text{params}}$)

Stores the model weights. For a model with $N$ parameters:

* **FP32 Precision**: $M_{\text{params}} = 4N \text{ bytes}$
* **FP16 / BF16 Mixed Precision**: $M_{\text{params}} = 2N \text{ bytes}$
* **8-Bit Quantized Baseline**: $M_{\text{params}} = 1N \text{ bytes}$

#### 2. Gradient Memory ($M_{\text{grads}}$)

Stores backpropagated gradients for all trainable parameters:

* **FP32 Gradients**: $M_{\text{grads}} = 4N \text{ bytes}$
* **FP16 / BF16 Gradients**: $M_{\text{grads}} = 2N \text{ bytes}$

#### 3. Optimizer State Memory ($M_{\text{opt}}$)

The optimizer maintains running historical moments for adaptive updates. For
standard AdamW:

* **Standard FP32 AdamW** (First moment $m_t$ + Second moment $v_t$ + Master
  FP32 weights):
  $$
  M_{\text{opt}} = 4N (m_t) + 4N (v_t) + 4N (\text{master copy}) = 12N \text{ bytes}
  $$
* **8-Bit AdamW (bitsandbytes)**:
  $$
  M_{\text{opt}} = 1N (m_t) + 1N (v_t) + 2N (\text{master copy}) = 4N \text{ bytes}
  $$
* **Adafactor / SGD with Momentum**:
  $$
  M_{\text{opt}} \approx 4N \text{ to } 8N \text{ bytes}
  $$

#### 4. Activation Memory ($M_{\text{activations}}$)

Stores intermediate forward tensors required during backpropagation:

* **Without Activation Checkpointing**:
  $$
  M_{\text{activations}} = B \cdot S \cdot L \cdot \left( 34 \cdot
  d_{\text{model}} + 5 \cdot a \cdot S \right) \text{ bytes}
  $$
  where $B$ is batch size, $S$ is sequence length, $L$ is layer count, and $a$
  is number of attention heads.
* **With Selective FlashAttention-2 & Activation Checkpointing**:
  Recomputes intermediate activations on the backward pass, reducing activation
  memory to:
  $$
  M_{\text{activations}} \approx \mathcal{O}(B \cdot S \cdot d_{\text{model}}
  \cdot \sqrt{L})
  $$

#### 5. Framework Workspace & CUDA Context ($M_{\text{workspace}}$)

CUDA driver contexts, PyTorch caching allocators, and temporary GEMM scratch
buffers allocate between $1.0\text{GB}$ and $2.5\text{GB}$ baseline memory.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_CODEFORMER.md` (CodeFormer: VQ-Codebook Face Restoration > 2. Visual Taxonomy: Discrete Codebook Prior):

The codebook $\mathcal{C} = \{c_k\}_{k=1}^K \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ consists of
$K = 1024$ learned discrete code vectors capturing high-frequency eye, skin, and
facial geometry primitives `[THEORETICAL]`. Features $z$ from degraded inputs
are mapped to their nearest codebook entries:

$$
z_q = \arg\min_{c_k \in \mathcal{C}} \|z - c_k\|_2
$$

CodeFormer introduces an adjustable modulation scalar $\alpha \in [0, 1]$
governing intermediate feature fusion:

$$
\tilde{F} = \alpha \cdot F_{\text{input}} + (1 - \alpha) \cdot F_{\text{codebook}}
$$

When $\alpha = 1.0$, identity preservation is maximized (biometric alignment);
when $\alpha = 0.0$, perceptual enhancement and de-noising are maximized.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_CODEFORMER.md` (CodeFormer: VQ-Codebook Face Restoration > 5. Challenges & Resilience Architecture):

Severe blind face restoration presents complex edge cases:

* **Extreme Occlusion & Eyeglasses**: Unconstrained continuous models
  hallucinate warped eyes behind heavy frames. CodeFormer's 9-layer Transformer
  predicts global contextual indices, utilizing unoccluded facial symmetry to
  anchor the discrete lookup.
* **Identity Drift vs. Detail Enhancement**: Sliding scalar $\alpha$ dynamically
  prevents synthetic over-sharpening from altering recognizable biometric facial
  features.
* **Publication-Grade FID 2048 & Memory Safety**: Validation computes Fréchet
  Inception Distance at standard feature dimension 2048 with micro-chunking
  ($b_{\text{chunk}} \le 2$), guaranteeing benchmark comparability against
  academic baselines while bounding evaluation VRAM to $< 280$ MB.
* **Monotonic Curriculum Ratchet & Dynamic Degradation**: Training strictly
  enforces monotonic data fraction expansion ($20\%$ strides) with on-the-fly
  degradation synthesis for containerized WebDatasets, preventing curriculum
  retreat and gradient starvation.
* **Sensor Readout Noise & JPEG Ringing**: Pre-flight degradation gating in the
  Dataset Compiler enforces high-fidelity Lanczos-3 rescales, training the
  codebook against realistic heteroscedastic noise distributions.

Forward noise injection follows the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck stochastic differential equation:

$$
dz = -\frac{1}{2} \beta(t) z dt + \sqrt{\beta(t)} dw

$$

#### 4.3.4 Performance Metrics & SOTA Targets

The training suite (v16.9.208) measures the single-box output per image; all
four targets are provisional (`sota_targets_provisional: true`): no cited
source backs them yet, and WIDER FACE easy / medium / hard AP does not apply

* **Box IoU (`box_iou`)**: mean IoU of the predicted and the labelled box over
  the images that hold a face. Target $\ge 0.80$.
* **AP50 (`ap50`)**: single-class AP over images (each image is one
  detection ranked by its confidence; a true positive holds a face and
  reaches IoU 0.5), all-point interpolated. Target $\ge 0.95$.
* **AP50-95 (`ap50_95`)**: the same AP averaged over the COCO thresholds
  0.50:0.05:0.95. Target $\ge 0.60$.
* **Landmark NME (`landmark_nme`)**: mean distance of the five points divided
  by the inter-ocular distance (points 0 and 1); lower is better. Target
  $\le 0.10$.

  without halo artifacts.

Explain the architectural design and implementation details of Universal Hybrid Restoration Pipelines > 3. Critical Architectural Optimizations > 3.2 Dynamic Filename Task Ingestion from PAPER_LEMGENDARY_HYBRID.

According to `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_HYBRID.md` (Universal Hybrid Restoration Pipelines > 3. Critical Architectural Optimizations > 3.2 Dynamic Filename Task Ingestion):

During dataset consolidation, multi-task models ingest millions of composite
images. A critical failure mode discovered was **Task-Index Blindness**, where
the loss engine received a static task label (e.g. `"restoration"` globally),
locking the routing classifier into a single head and halting the optimization
of secondary heads.

We implemented the **Dynamic Task-Index Extractor**:

- Instantiates a regex-driven analysis of compiled physical image filenames via
  `professionalmultitaskrestoration_[task]_compiled_[manifold]_[idx].jpg`.
- Maps physical compilation tags (`deblur`, `denoise`, `derain`,
  `dehaze_indoor`, `dehaze_outdoor`, `lowlight`, `exposure`, `superres`,
  `vintage`, `face_restorer`, and `face_parser`) natively back to task indices
  with backward-compatible substring fallbacks.
- Passes explicit `task_idx` targets to the `CombinedLoss` CrossEntropy
  classifier during training, forcing proper multi-head optimization.
  The `CombinedLoss` engine normalizes both collated string tuples, single
  strings, and integer tensors into strict $\text{int64}$ target tensors
  ($\mathbf{y}_{\text{task}} \in \{0, \dots, 10\}^B$), preventing collation
  type mismatches and driving both auxiliary cross-entropy loss and dynamic
  perceptual weight scaling:
  $$
  \mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \mathcal{L}_1 + 0.1 \cdot
  \mathcal{L}_{\text{CE}}(\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{\text{task}},
  \mathbf{y}_{\text{task}}) + \frac{1}{B} \sum_{i=1}^B
  w_{\text{LPIPS}}[\mathbf{y}_{\text{task}, i}] \cdot \mathcal{L}_{\text{perc},
  i}
  $$

To support both cloud-scale **Kaggle TPU v5e-8** (`TpuV5E8`, 8 cores, 128 GB
aggregate HBM2e, native `bfloat16` MXUs) and local **4 GB VRAM** consumer GPUs
without maintaining separate model codebases, `GenericCausalLLM` and
`InstructionDataset` implement a dual-regime execution architecture:

1. **Device-Adaptive Precision & Quantization**:
   * **Kaggle TPU v5e-8**: Automatically disables CUDA-only `bitsandbytes` 4-bit
     quantization (`load_in_4bit = False`) and loads the backbone in native
     `torch.bfloat16` with `lora_r = 32`, `lora_alpha = 64`, and
     rank-stabilized LoRA (`use_rslora = True`, scaling updates by
     $\alpha / \sqrt{r}$).
   * **Local 4 GB GPU**: Enforces 4-bit NormalFloat (`nf4`) double quantization
     with hardware-verified compute dtype (`bfloat16` on Ampere+, `float16` on
     Turing), `lora_r = 8`, and `batch_size = 1` with `accumulation_steps = 16`.
2. **Chunked Linear Cross-Entropy (`ChunkedCausalLMLoss`)**:
   * Standard `AutoModelForCausalLM.forward(labels=...)` materializes the full
     $[B, S, V]$ logit tensor ($V = 151,936$ for Qwen2.5) and upcasts it to
     FP32, consuming $\sim 778\text{ MB}$ at $B=1, S=512$ and $>3\text{ GB}$ at
     $B=2, S=1024$.

     (`labels != -100`) and projects `lm_head` in chunks of $C \in \{256, 1024\}$
     with non-reentrant gradient checkpointing, reducing peak output-layer
     memory by $>94\%$.

     `pred_ids` ($[B, S]$) instead of $[B, S, V]$ floating-point logits.

     enforces invariant $[B, S]$ tensor shapes so the PyTorch/XLA PJRT compiler

4. **SOTA Corpus Curation & Decontamination**:

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_LLM.md` (Large Language Models & Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) > 6. Parameter Specifications & Scaling > 6.6 Edge Hardware Optimization: 4-Bit NF4 QLoRA, SDPA & Paged AdamW):

To execute fine-tuning of 1.5B+ parameter causal language models on consumer
workstations constrained to 4 GB VRAM (e.g. NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650), the
training suite deploys a multi-tier memory containment profile:

1. **NormalFloat-4 (NF4) Quantization**: Employs `bitsandbytes` 4-bit normal
   quantization with double quantization (`bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True`),
   compressing FP32/BF16 base foundation weights from 3.1 GB to ~900 MB while
   retaining near-lossless numerical fidelity.
2. **Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA)**: Injects rank $r=16$, $\alpha=32$ adapters
   across all projection matrices ($q$, $k$, $v$, $o$, $\text{gate}$,
   $\text{up}$, $\text{down}$), training $<1\%$ of total network weights.
3. **Gradient Checkpointing & SDPA**: Recomputes activations during backward
   passes via `model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(use_reentrant=False)` and
   substitutes manual attention matrices with PyTorch Scaled Dot-Product
   Attention (`attn_implementation="sdpa"`).
4. **Paged 8-bit AdamW**: Leverages `bitsandbytes.optim.PagedAdamW8bit` to
   compress optimizer states to 8 bits and dynamically page optimizer states
   across CUDA unified memory when VRAM boundaries approach saturation.
5. **Sequence Clamping**: Constrains micro-batch to 1 and sequence length to 512
   tokens with 16 gradient accumulation steps, eliminating $O(N^2)$ memory spikes
   and preserving stable throughput on edge accelerators.

Positional encoding uses Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE), rotating query and
key vectors in complex 2D planes to naturally capture relative distance:

$$
R_{\Theta, m}^d = \text{diag}(R_{\theta_1, m}, R_{\theta_2, m}, \dots,
R_{\theta_{d/2}, m})
$$

Feed-Forward networks replace standard GELU with SwiGLU (Swish Gated Linear
Units, Shazeer 2020), projecting inputs through independent gate ($W_1$) and
value ($W_2$) matrices before down-projection ($W_3$):

$$
\text{SwiGLU}(x) = \left( \text{Swish}(x W_1) \odot (x W_2) \right) W_3 = \left(
(x W_1 \cdot \sigma(x W_1)) \odot (x W_2) \right) W_3
$$

evaluation metrics:

1. **Perplexity ($\text{PPL}$)**: Evaluates confidence on validation tokens:

   $$
   \text{PPL} = \exp\left( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \mathcal{L}_i \right)

   \hat{y}_i = y_i \right) \cdot \mathbb{I}\left( y_i \ne -100 \right)}
   {\sum_{i=1}^{M} \mathbb{I}\left( y_i \ne -100 \right)} \times 100\%
   $$

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_LLM.md` (Large Language Models & Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) > 6. Parameter Specifications & Scaling > 6.1 QLoRA Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning & Dynamic Quantization):

For consumer hardware deployment (e.g. NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 with 4GB VRAM),
full parameter fine-tuning of 1.5B dense transformers is intractable. The suite
deploys **QLoRA (Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation)** utilizing NF4 (NormalFloat4)
weight quantization with double quantization and 16-bit LoRA adapter matrices
injected across projection layers (`q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj`, `o_proj`,
`gate_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj`):

$$
W_{\text{eff}} = W_{\text{NF4}} + \frac{\alpha}{r} (B \cdot A)
$$

where rank $r=16$, $\alpha=32$, and LoRA dropout is $0.05$. NF4 loading is
opt-in: `GenericCausalLLM` quantizes only when `load_in_4bit=True` is passed
(default `False`); otherwise the LoRA adapters sit on a bfloat16 base on CUDA.

According to `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_LLM.md` (Large Language Models & Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) > 6. Parameter Specifications & Scaling > 6.2 Hardware-Aware Dynamic Micro-Batch & Gradient Accumulation Scaling):

Memory sentinels probe free VRAM at runtime. To prevent Out-Of-Memory (OOM)
faults while maintaining a stable target effective batch size
($B_{\text{eff}} = 24$), physical micro-batch size ($B_{\text{phys}}$) and
gradient accumulation steps ($K_{\text{accum}}$) are resolved dynamically:

$$
K_{\text{accum}} = \max\left(1, \operatorname{round}\left(
\frac{B_{\text{eff}}}{B_{\text{phys}}} \right)\right)
$$

On 4GB hardware, $B_{\text{phys}} = 2$ and $K_{\text{accum}} = 12$, yielding an
effective batch of 24 with peak activation memory constrained below 2.8 GB
(a sizing target; `ai_helper_lemgend` pins `batch_size: 2` and
`accumulation_steps: 12` in `unified_models_v2.yaml`, and the code does not
measure the 2.8 GB bound).

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_LLM.md` (Large Language Models & Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) > 6. Parameter Specifications & Scaling > 6.3 Token Accuracy & Autoregressive Validation Formulations):

Validation loss ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{val}}$) is complemented by two primary
evaluation metrics:

1. **Perplexity ($\text{PPL}$)**: Evaluates confidence on validation tokens:

   $$
   \text{PPL} = \exp\left( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \mathcal{L}_i \right)
   $$

2. **Non-Masked Token Accuracy ($\text{Acc}_{\text{token}}$)**: Evaluates
   next-token prediction correctness exclusively over assistant target turns,
   ignoring prompt tokens masked with $-100$:

   $$
   \text{Acc}_{\text{token}} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{M} \mathbb{I}\left(
   \hat{y}_i = y_i \right) \cdot \mathbb{I}\left( y_i \ne -100 \right)}
   {\sum_{i=1}^{M} \mathbb{I}\left( y_i \ne -100 \right)} \times 100\%
   $$

Imagine taking photos in almost pitch-black darkness or on an intensely sunny
beach where parts of the image are completely blown out:

- **Dual-Track Illumination Recovery:** MIRNet v2 operates across two difficult
  lighting regimes: pulling sharp, colorful images out of near-black shadows,
  and recovering highlight texture from overexposed skies.
- **Parallel Multi-Scale Streams:** Rather than shrinking the image down and
  guessing missing fine details on the way back up, MIRNet processes
  full-resolution, medium, and low-scale streams in parallel, allowing crisp
  textures and broad exposure corrections to communicate continuously.
- **Zero Grainy Noise Amplification:** It brightens dim subjects naturally
  without blowing up the ugly multi-colored sensor grain typical of night-mode
  camera processing.

According to `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_MPRNET.md` (High-Fidelity MPRNet Deraining via SOTA Infrastructure > 2. Visual Taxonomy `[THEORETICAL]`: The LemGendary Restoration Subset > 2.2 Multi-Stage Progressive Operators (CSFF & SAM)):

To handle severe torrential rain streaks and refractive drops without losing
structural sharpness, MPRNet utilizes a multi-stage architecture
($S_1, S_2, S_3$) equipped with Cross-Stage Feature Fusion (CSFF) and Supervised
Attention Modules (SAM):

- **Cross-Stage Feature Fusion (CSFF)**:
  Features from earlier encoder-decoder stages ($S_{k-1}$) are dynamically fused
  into the subsequent stage ($S_k$) to prevent spatial detail degradation across
  multi-scale downsampling. For feature tensor $F^{k-1}$ from stage $k-1$ and
  feature tensor $F^k$ from stage $k$:

  $$
  F_{\text{fused}}^k = F^k + \Phi_{k-1 \to k}\left( \text{Conv}_{1\times
  1}(F^{k-1}) \right)
  $$

  where $\Phi_{k-1 \to k}(\cdot)$ denotes spatial rescalers (up/downsampling
  convolutions) aligning spatial dimensions $H \times W$.

- **Supervised Attention Module (SAM)**:
  Instead of propagating raw intermediate predictions, SAM generates stage-wise
  spatial attention maps $M^k \in [0, 1]^{1 \times H \times W}$ slaved directly
  to intermediate residual targets:

  $$
  M^k = \sigma\left( \text{Conv}_{1\times 1}\left( \delta\left(
  \text{Conv}_{3\times 3}(\hat{I}^k) \right) \right) \right)
  $$

  $$
  F_{\text{attended}}^k = F^k \odot M^k + F^k
  $$

  where $\hat{I}^k$ is the intermediate RGB reconstruction at stage $k$,
  $\sigma(\cdot)$ is the sigmoid function, and $\odot$ represents element-wise
  Hadamard multiplication.

- **Progressive Stage-Wise Loss Formulation**:
  Total loss is computed as a weighted summation across all 3 stages:

  $$
  \mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \sum_{k=1}^3 \left( \|\hat{I}^k -
  I_{\text{gt}}\|_1 + \lambda_{\text{edge}} \mathcal{L}_{\text{edge}}(\hat{I}^k,
  I_{\text{gt}}) \right) + \lambda_{\text{perceptual}}
  \mathcal{L}_{\text{LPIPS}}(\hat{I}^3, I_{\text{gt}})
  $$

  where $\mathcal{L}_{\text{edge}}$ computes the Charbonnier loss over
  horizontal and vertical gradient fields $\Delta \hat{I}^k$.

`torch.cuda.mem_get_info()`. This ensures that even on 4GB hardware, the MPRNet
architecture is seated with a perfectly calculated physical batch size,
preventing kernel-level address misalignments and system-wide paging.

#### 3.1.2 OVC Data Streaming Bridge (OpenCV-to-CUDA)

The pipeline harnesses local NumPy/OpenCV workers to decode image tensors
natively in CPU cache before flushing them to the GPU. This prevents
data-starvation of the GPU cores completely, hiding I/O latency behind raw
throughput.

#### 3.2.3 PCIe VRAM Thrashing & The Chunking Fix

When attempting to validate a subset of $N$ images ($N = 425$), passing all
tensors to the perceptual networks simultaneously causes VRAM utilization to
scale as:

$$

this immediately shatters the physical memory limit, prompting the operating
system to initiate paging over the PCIe bus (VRAM-to-System-RAM swapping), which
causes severe latency.

Imagine taking an action photo that came out completely blurred because your
hands shook, or a low-light snapshot covered in rough speckled noise:

- **Nonlinear Activation-Free Design:** Conventional neural networks use complex
  non-linear functions (like GELU or ReLU) that slow down calculation. NAFNet
  proves you don't need them: it replaces heavy operations with simple
  element-wise multiplications (SimpleGate), making it blazing fast.
- **Dual Deblurring & Denoising Power:** In a single unified model family, it
  fixes camera motion blur (restoring crisp readable text and distinct
  eyelashes) and wipes away digital sensor grain.
- **High Efficiency for Browser Runtimes:** Because its building blocks are so
  simple, NAFNet runs smoothly inside WebGPU-accelerated browsers without
  burning through computer memory.

Explain the architectural design and implementation details of High-Fidelity NIMA Assessment via Hardware-Aware Optimization > 5. Challenges & Resilience Architecture > 5.47 Differentiable Soft-Spearman Loss & Cross-Microbatch Rank Memory Bank (v19.0) from PAPER_LEMGENDARY_NIMA.

According to `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_NIMA.md` (High-Fidelity NIMA Assessment via Hardware-Aware Optimization > 5. Challenges & Resilience Architecture > 5.47 Differentiable Soft-Spearman Loss & Cross-Microbatch Rank Memory Bank (v19.0)):

Under constrained edge hardware (GTX 1650 4GB @ 512px), physical micro-batch
size $b=2$ creates a severe pairwise ranking bottleneck. While Earth Mover's
Distance (EMD) loss optimizes linear density correlation (driving
$\text{PLCC} \ge 0.9102$), evaluating only $\binom{2}{2} = 1$ pair per step
starves monotonic rank gradients, stalling $\text{SRCC}$ at $\sim 0.8178$.

To eliminate this bottleneck, the v19.0 architecture integrates:

1. **Differentiable Soft-Spearman Loss**: Computes smooth surrogate ranks via
   temperature-scaled logistic sigmoids:
   $$
   \tilde{r}_i^p = 1 + \sum_{j \ne i} \frac{1}{1 + \exp\left(-\frac{p_i - p_j}{\tau}\right)}
   $$
2. **Cross-Microbatch Rank Memory Bank**: A detached FIFO queue ($N=32$) caches
   recent predictions and targets across gradient accumulation cycles. On every
   forward step, active predictions are concatenated with memory bank tensors,
   computing pairwise rank correlation across $\binom{32}{2} = 496$ sample
   pairs.

The hallmark of the LemGendary project is its departure from pure Earth Mover's
Distance (EMD).

#### 3.1.1 Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) - The Histogram Anchor

The primary loss function aligns the predicted probability distribution of
scores (1–10) with the rater ground truth. This ensures the model understands
not just a "mean score," but the rater agreement/disagreement for an image.

#### 3.1.2 True Rank Correlation via EMD Temperature Anchoring

Initially, the suite experimented with a differentiable **PLCC-Penalty** to
proxy rank-order (SRCC). However, empirical analysis revealed that batch-wise
PLCC forces predictions to symmetrically center around the *small batch's mean*,
destructively scrambling global rank order. Thus, the PLCC penalty was
**banned**. Instead, SRCC stability is achieved by retaining pure **Earth
Mover's Distance (EMD)** augmented with a strict **0.1 Temperature Anchor** on
the softmax probabilities, ensuring rank preservation without batch-level
fluctuation.
$$
Loss_{Resonance} = Loss_{EMD(Temperature=0.1)}
$$

Superseded since Training Suite v16.9.186: NIMA models train at temperature
1 with the paper EMD and a soft logit cap (Section 5.50).

#### 3.1.3 The Resonance Coefficient Selection (0.15 Weighting)

The **0.15 coefficient** was empirically selected to balance the "EMD
Convergence" (absolute score accuracy) with "Ranking Integrity." A higher weight
causes the model to ignore score distributions in favor of order, while a lower
weight results in "Score Flipping." At 0.15, the model maintains ordinal
stability even on near-identical technical artifacts.

#### 3.1.4 The Soft-Label PMF Strategy

To achieve high-fidelity convergence, scores are not treated as flat scalars
(e.g., 7.5). Instead, they are transformed into a **Probability Mass Function
(PMF)** over the 1-10 range. This allows the EMD loss to "feel" the shape of
human consensus, teaching the model to distinguish between a "solid 7.0" and a
"highly controversial 7.0."

According to `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_NIMA.md` (High-Fidelity NIMA Assessment via Hardware-Aware Optimization > 5. Challenges & Resilience Architecture > 5.45 SRCC-Driven Dynamic Governance & Rank Margin Ceiling Calibration (v18.0)):

**Issue**: In previous Governor iterations, the autonomous hyperparameter
booster in `optimization_engine.py` audited `plcc` against the target SOTA
threshold (`plcc < target_srcc`), erroneously using the linear correlation
metric as a proxy for Spearman rank-order correlation (`SRCC`). In late-stage
refinement (such as `nima_technical` at 512px), linear correlation saturated at
$\text{PLCC} \ge 0.9100$ while rank-order correlation lingered around
$\text{SRCC} \approx 0.8170$. Because `plcc` had already crossed the target
threshold, the Governor prematurely suppressed rank-weight boosting, capping
`rank_weight` at `1.5` and leaving the ranking loss gradient unable to push SRCC
past the ~0.82 plateau.

**Fix**: Executed the **v18.0 SOTA Rank Alignment Upgrade**:

1. **Explicit SRCC Parameter Binding**: Updated `audit_epoch` signature in
   `optimization_engine.py` and both invocation sites in `train.py` to pass the
   live `srcc=srcc` metric directly into the decision engine.
2. **True Rank-Order Trigger**: The autonomous boost condition now directly
   monitors `srcc < target_srcc`, ensuring rank boosting activates whenever rank
   correlation lags, regardless of PLCC saturation.
3. **Configurable Ceiling & Floor Governance**: Decoupled hardcoded limits by
   introducing `max_rank_weight` (up to `2.0`) and `min_rank_margin` (`0.05`) in
   model stabilizers (`unified_models_v2.yaml`), allowing the Governor to
   dynamically scale ranking gradients up to 2.0x while safely maintaining
   margin tightening down to the exact 0.05 target floor.

Training Suite v16.9.162 and v16.9.186 supersede the temperature anchoring of
Sections 3.1.2 and 5.40 for every NIMA model:

- **Logit soft cap**: the hard `torch.clamp(logits, -10, 10)` is replaced by
  $\text{cap} \cdot \tanh(\text{logits} / \text{cap})$ with the registry
  `stabilizers.logit_clamp` (15.0 for every NIMA entry; 0 turns it off). Every
  score bin stays differentiable.
- **Temperature 1**: quality models train at temperature 1 under that cap
  (`PinnedThermalState`, `PinnedCalibration`); sharpening, recoil, resets and
  checkpoint restore leave the temperature at 1.0, and the quality loss is a
  plain softmax.
- **EMD form**: `stabilizers.emd_form` is `nima` (default, the paper's r = 2
  form per sample, then the batch mean) or `squared`; the five NIMA entries
  set `nima`. Checkpoints record `emd_form`, a resume keeps the recorded form
  (older NIMA checkpoints keep `legacy_sum`), and the form is a frozen run
  setting.
- **Post-hoc calibration**: `python -m training.quality_calibration
  val_scores.npz` fits one temperature on validation logits (grid 0.5 to
  2.0, lowest EMD) and keeps it only when PLCC and SRCC do not drop. An
  accepted value is stored as the registry `calibration.temperature` and used
  by the export `SoftmaxWrapper` (default 1.0).

Training massive architectures like **EfficientNetV2-S** at high resolutions
requires surgical VRAM management across diverse hardware targets.

#### 3.2.1 The Headroom-Aware Memory-Sentinel

The Sentinel has evolved from a static lookup table to an **Active Probing
Engine**. Instead of assuming a fixed capacity, it invokes
`torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` (or backend equivalents) to sense the true available
headroom. This accounts for browser tabs, OS compositors, and external GPU
tasks, ensuring that the physical batch size is always seated within the safe
"Non-Paging" manifold.

#### 3.2.2 Intra-Epoch Paging Protection

To handle dynamic system load (e.g., opening a browser mid-training), the suite
implements an **Intra-Epoch VRAM Sentinel**. By probing free memory every 50
batches, the system can preemptively halt the training loop and downscale the
physical batch size (compensating with gradient accumulation) before a
kernel-level paging event occurs.

#### 3.2.3 OVC Data Streaming Bridge (OpenCV-to-CUDA)

To minimize latency on the PCIe 3.0 bus, the suite uses the **OVC Bridge**.
Images are pre-processed in the CPU's L3 cache using OpenCV's optimized SIMD
instructions before being mapped directly into the GPU's memory buffer. This
"Prefetch-and-Map" strategy hides the I/O latency of the high-fidelity samples,
ensuring the kernels are never starved for data.

According to `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_NIMA.md` (High-Fidelity NIMA Assessment via Hardware-Aware Optimization > 5. Challenges & Resilience Architecture > 5.41 Head Projection Upgrade & Resolution Ladder Expansion (v16.1)):

**Issue**: The `nima_aesthetic_mobile` model uses a bare
`Dropout(0.5) → Linear(1280, 10)` classification head. This single linear
mapping from the MobileNetV3-Small feature space directly to 10 score bins
provides insufficient representational capacity for aesthetic quality
assessment, resulting in a hard PLCC ceiling around 0.47 despite the backbone
being fully converged.

Additionally, the `res_ladder` config contained only `[224]`, preventing the
Governor from ever triggering the `DEEPENING` phase (a spatial resolution jump).
The model spent 95+ epochs at a single resolution without any opportunity to
learn higher-frequency spatial features.

**Fix**: Two complementary changes applied to unlock further capacity:

1. **Hidden Projection Layer** (`nima.py`, Governor v16.1): Added an optional
   `hidden_dim` parameter to `NIMA_Model`. When set to `256` via `kwargs` in the
   YAML, the head becomes
   `Dropout(0.5) → Linear(1280, 256) → GELU → Dropout(0.25) → Linear(256, 10)`.
   This intermediate manifold allows the model to learn richer aesthetic
   representations before collapsing to 10 bins. The change is
   backwards-compatible: all other NIMA variants default to `hidden_dim=None`
   and are completely unaffected. The checkpoint loader uses `strict=False`, so
   the pretrained MobileNetV3-Small backbone weights are fully preserved and
   only the new head is randomly initialized on the next restart.

2. **Resolution Ladder Expansion** (`unified_models_v2.yaml`): Expanded
   `res_ladder` for `nima_aesthetic_mobile` from `[224]` to `[224, 256]`,
   enabling the Governor's spatial jump mechanism to trigger a `DEEPENING` phase
   at 256px once the 224px performance has plateaued.

According to `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_NIMA.md` (High-Fidelity NIMA Assessment via Hardware-Aware Optimization > 5. Challenges & Resilience Architecture > 5.39 Max Stress LR Freeze Fix (Governor v16)):

**Issue**: A logic gap in the Governor's `REFINEMENT` phase. When
`current_stress` reached the maximum level of `5.0` and the model's quality
score was still far below `target_quality_score * 0.90`, the code fell through
to the `else` branch and applied `cooling_factor` (0.85×) to the LR every single
epoch. After 30–40 epochs at max stress, the LR was crushed to near-zero,
completely freezing the model's ability to escape the local minimum. The SOTA
deactivation gate (which resets stress) only fires when quality *improves*,
creating an unescapable deadlock.

**Observed In**: `nima_aesthetic_mobile` — 86 epochs, stress=5.0 from epoch 83+,
PLCC stuck at 0.47 vs. target 0.60, LR decaying exponentially from 5e-5 toward
the 1e-5 absolute floor.

**Fix**: Added a new `elif` branch (Governor v16) in `optimization_engine.py`
between the stress-escalation block and the cooling fallback. When
`current_stress >= 5.0` and the model is still far from SOTA, the LR is forced
to `jolt_multiplier` (1.5×) instead of the cooling factor, maintaining momentum.
A new `max_stress_stuck_epochs` counter (persisted in `get_state`/`load_state`)
tracks how long the model has been at max stress with no improvement. After
`plateau_patience × 2` epochs in this state, a `[STUCK]` signal is emitted to
notify the operator that the architecture may be at its representational
capacity.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_NIMA.md` (High-Fidelity NIMA Assessment via Hardware-Aware Optimization > 5. Challenges & Resilience Architecture > 5.48 Spatial Statistical Pooling Upgrade (Mean ⊕ Std) for Micro-Defect Localization):

Global Average Pooling (GAP) calculates $\frac{1}{HW}\sum x_{h,w}$, which
attenuates high-frequency localized micro-defects (e.g. ISO grain, compression
ringing) when defects occupy only a fraction of the 512px canvas.

The upgraded NIMA head adopts dual-moment statistical pooling:
$$
\mu_c = \frac{1}{HW} \sum_{h,w} x_{c,h,w}, \quad \sigma_c = \sqrt{\frac{1}{HW}
\sum_{h,w} (x_{c,h,w} - \mu_c)^2 + \epsilon}
$$
$$
\text{Pooling}_{\text{stats}}(x) = [\mu_1, \dots, \mu_C, \sigma_1, \dots,
\sigma_C]^T \in \mathbb{R}^{2C}
$$
This doubles feature sensitivity to localized high-frequency texture variations
without altering convolutional backbone weights.

According to `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_NIMA.md` (High-Fidelity NIMA Assessment via Hardware-Aware Optimization > 5. Challenges & Resilience Architecture > 5.48 Spatial Statistical Pooling Upgrade (Mean ⊕ Std) for Micro-Defect Localization):

Global Average Pooling (GAP) calculates $\frac{1}{HW}\sum x_{h,w}$, which
attenuates high-frequency localized micro-defects (e.g. ISO grain, compression
ringing) when defects occupy only a fraction of the 512px canvas.

The upgraded NIMA head adopts dual-moment statistical pooling:
$$
\mu_c = \frac{1}{HW} \sum_{h,w} x_{c,h,w}, \quad \sigma_c = \sqrt{\frac{1}{HW}
\sum_{h,w} (x_{c,h,w} - \mu_c)^2 + \epsilon}
$$
$$
\text{Pooling}_{\text{stats}}(x) = [\mu_1, \dots, \mu_C, \sigma_1, \dots,
\sigma_C]^T \in \mathbb{R}^{2C}
$$
This doubles feature sensitivity to localized high-frequency texture variations
without altering convolutional backbone weights.

> **Heuristic Classification**: The scalar Restoration Quality Score defined

#### Empirical Weighting & Normalization Rationale

* **$\text{PSNR}$ (Scale factor $1.0$)**: Provides global pixel-level intensity
  fidelity in decibels ($\text{dB}$), typically ranging from $20.0$ to $50.0$.

* **$\text{SSIM} \times 20$ (Scale factor $20.0$)**: Maps structural similarity
  (bounded $[0, 1]$) into a $[0, 20]$ interval, making a $\Delta 0.05$
  structural difference equivalent to $\Delta 1.0\text{ dB}$ PSNR.
* **$-\text{LPIPS} \times 20$ (Scale factor $-20.0$)**: Maps deep perceptual
  patch distance (bounded $[0, 1]$, lower is better) into a $[-20, 0]$ penalty,
  penalizing perceptual artifacts proportionally to structural gains.
* **Convergence Target**: Convergence ladders treat scores $\ge 50.0$ as
  entry-level fidelity, $\ge 60.0$ as production-grade, and $\ge 65.0$ as
  benchmark state-of-the-art.

training suite measures RetinaFace with four metrics (v16.9.224,
`training/training/face_detection_metrics.py`). The targets are calibrated
against standard single-shot face localisation benchmarks:

* **Box IoU (`box_iou`)**: mean IoU of the predicted and the labelled box over
  the images that hold a face. Target $\ge 0.72$ `[TARGET]`.
* **AP50 (`ap50`)**: single-class AP over images; each image is one detection
  ranked by its confidence (used as returned, no second sigmoid) and is a
  true positive when it holds a face and the IoU reaches 0.5. Target
  $\ge 0.95$ `[TARGET]`.
* **AP50-95 (`ap50_95`)**: the same AP averaged over the COCO thresholds
  0.50:0.05:0.95. Target $\ge 0.60$ `[TARGET]`.
* **Landmark NME (`landmark_nme`)**: mean distance of the five points divided
  by the inter-ocular distance (points 0 and 1); box-only labels are left
  out. Target $\le 0.05$ `[TARGET]`.
* **Measured values**: not measured on the rebuilt labels yet.

According to `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_UPN_V2.md` (UPN v2: Universal Parameterized Network > 3. Shared Foundations: Feature Modulation & Multi-Objective Optimization):

The core structural element of UPN v2 is the Feature Modulation Block (FMB). Let
$F \in \mathbb{R}^{C  \times H  \times W}$ denote intermediate feature
representations:

$$
\text{FMB}(F, \mathbf{z}) = \gamma(\mathbf{z}) \odot \left( \frac{F - \mu(F)}{\sigma(F)}
\right) + \beta(\mathbf{z})
$$

where $\gamma(\cdot)$ and $\beta(\cdot)$ are affine projection networks that map
$\mathbf{z}$ to channel-wise scale and bias vectors. Training couples spatial
errors, perceptual discrepancies, and parameter gradient smoothness:

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \rho(\hat{I} - I_{ \text{clean}}) + \lambda_{
\text{perc}} \mathcal{L}_{ \text{VGG}}(\hat{I}, I_{ \text{clean}}) + \lambda_{
\text{grad}} \|
\nabla_{\mathbf{z}} \mathcal{F}_{\theta}(I, \mathbf{z})\|_2
$$

The gradient penalty ensures that minute changes in the steering parameter
$\mathbf{z}$ yield smooth, Lipschitz-bounded modifications to the restored
output.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_LEMGENDARY_YOLOV8N.md` (YOLOv8n Multi-Task Perception Architecture > 5. Challenges & Resilience Architecture > 5.2. Checkpoint Resumption & Multi-Fraction Progress Recovery (v16.9.13)):

Prior to v16.9.13, initiating training with pre-existing weights could risk
restarting the epoch counter or jumping across resolutions prematurely. The
v16.9.13 Resumption Protocol provides rigorous multi-fraction checkpoint
inspection and mid-stage resumption:

1. **Deep Checkpoint & State Inspection**: Loads candidate checkpoints
   (`torch.load(..., map_location="cpu")`) to interrogate training metadata,
   including `epoch` (last completed epoch), `train_args.imgsz` (resolution
   rung), `train_args.fraction` (dataset fraction), and `train_args.epochs`
   (target epochs).
2. **Completed Stage Skipping**: If a checkpoint or `metrics.csv` indicates that
   stage $k$ (e.g. $320\text{px}$ at $30\%$ fraction) has been superseded, that
   is, training has progressed to a higher fraction or higher resolution rung (a
   stage is never considered complete by epoch count), the governor logs
   completion and skips directly to the active ladder stage without redundant
   iterations.
3. **Mid-Stage Seamless Resumption**: If an interrupted run is detected on the
   active stage (matching resolution and fraction), the governor stages
   `last.pt`, restores optimizer, scaler and EMA state through
   `trainer._load_checkpoint_state`, and continues from global epoch
   $\text{ckpt\_epoch} + 2$. `resume = True` is deliberately not used because
   Ultralytics would reset the epoch budget to the previous stage-local value.
4. **Global Epoch Synchronization**: Epochs are monotonic across all stages. The
   governor injects `trainer.start_epoch` and `trainer.epochs` at
   `on_pretrain_routine_end` and aligns the learning-rate scheduler, so the
   Ultralytics progress bar, the Governor banner
   (`Global Epoch N/M | Stage k/13 | Rung Epoch r | Plateau Watch s/5`),
   `metrics.csv` and WebSocket telemetry report identical epoch numbers.
5. **Validation Progress Display**: The validator description is overridden to
   `Validation`, replacing the raw metric column header in the progress bar, and
   an epoch summary line reports train loss, validation loss (box, cls, dfl),
   mAP50 and mAP50-95 at every epoch end.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_TRAINING_PATHOLOGY.md` (Nuclear Stability: AI Training Pathology Master Guide > 4. Modern 2026 Pathologies > PCIe Paging Thrashing & Host VRAM Starvation on 4GB Accelerators (Pathology 34)):

Two workloads hit the same 4 GB paging limit: 4-bit language models with long
sequences, and vision models whose batches exceed the free VRAM (formerly
Pathology 47, the Sub-Nuclear 4GB Lockdown).

- **The Issue**: On edge GPUs with 4 GB physical VRAM (e.g. NVIDIA GTX 1650),
  ambient OS, display managers, and hardware-accelerated host applications (e.g.
  Chrome, Photoshop) claim ~450–600 MB of Dedicated VRAM. While a 1.5B 4-bit
  model fits in ~1,600 MB at rest, processing long sequence lengths (e.g. 1024
  tokens) with standard AdamW and uncheckpointed activations pushes total
  allocation past the 4 GB boundary. The WDDM GPU driver dynamically pages active
  tensor allocations over the PCIe 3.0 bus to system RAM, causing batch step
  latency to balloon from ~1.5s up to 25s+ per iteration.
- **Identification**: `nvidia-smi` reports 100% GPU utilization with VRAM pegged
  at >3,600 MB, high CPU/PCIe bus activity, and fluctuating batch times (13.9s ->
  22.7s).
- **Remedy**: **Multi-Tier VRAM Containment Profile**. Deploy 4-bit NF4 base
  quantization via `BitsAndBytesConfig`, enable activation gradient checkpointing
  (`gradient_checkpointing_enable(use_reentrant=False)`), wire
  `bitsandbytes.optim.PagedAdamW8bit` for dynamic host paging without bus lockups,
  and clamp sequence lengths to 512 tokens with micro-batch size 1 and 16
  accumulation steps for edge training.
- **The Issue (Vision Models)**: 4GB cards (GTX 1650) trigger **System RAM
  Paging** when VRAM usage exceeds ~3.5GB, slowing training by 10x-20x.
- **Identification (Vision Models)**: "Shared GPU Memory" in Task Manager
  exceeds 1GB; speed drops below 0.5 img/s.
- **Remedy (Vision Models)**: **Absolute Sentinel Authority**. The Memory
  Sentinel now acts as the absolute physical authority, overriding any
  hardcoded YAML config batch sizes. It dynamically clamps pixel volumes to
  fit entirely within physical VRAM, preventing Windows System RAM paging.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_TRAINING_PATHOLOGY.md` (Nuclear Stability: AI Training Pathology Master Guide > 4. Modern 2026 Pathologies > Multitask Target Collation Type Mismatch & Loss Crash (Pathology 35)):

- **The Issue**: In multi-task image restoration models such as
  `professional_multitask_restoration`, DataLoader pipelines ingest sample
  metadata containing textual task tags (e.g. `"deblur"`, `"derain"`,
  `"dehaze_indoor"`) rather than pre-indexed scalar integers. Standard PyTorch
  DataLoader collation collects heterogeneous string targets into Python
  tuples of strings (`tuple[str, ...]`) for each batch. When passed directly
  to PyTorch loss functions like `nn.CrossEntropyLoss`, the engine attempts
  to execute `torch._C._nn.cross_entropy_loss(pred, target)`, which requires
  the target parameter to be a `torch.Tensor` of class indices or probabilities.
  Because the target remains a string tuple, the training loop crashes at step 1
  with:
  `TypeError: cross_entropy_loss(): argument 'target' (position 2) must be`
  `Tensor, not tuple`.
- **Identification**: Training starts cleanly, allocates GPU memory, resolves
  WebDataset/Tar readers, and prints `Initiating training pass...`, but crashes
  on the first optimization step with `TypeError: cross_entropy_loss(): argument
  'target' (position 2) must be Tensor, not tuple` inside `CombinedLoss.forward`
  or `F.cross_entropy`.
- **Remedy**: **Canonical Multitask Target Index Tensor Resolution**.
  1. Define a centralized, authoritative registry of task head names
     (`MULTITASK_HEAD_NAMES`) and a mapping from name to integer class index
     (`MULTITASK_HEAD_TO_INDEX`).
  2. Implement an idempotent resolution function
     (`_resolve_task_index_tensor`) inside `CombinedLoss` that handles:
     - Pre-existing scalar/1D/2D integer tensors (clamped and moved to device).
     - Collated tuples or lists of task name strings, resolving each via
       authoritative lookup or regex keyword parsing (`multitask_head(name)`).
     - Individual string values, converted into a single-element batch tensor.
  3. Ensure that `dataset_containers.py` dynamically resolves the sub-task head
     for `professional_multitask_restoration` items from filename prefixes or
     container sample IDs rather than falling back to a static generic label.

  errors generate an irreducible ~1,400 pip loss gradient per batch, inflating
  validation loss from ~9.3 to 232+ and locking TP/SL MAE at 1,415–1,440 pips.

  $T \le 0.14$ scales low signal-to-noise financial logits by $7\times$, causing
  severe probability overconfidence and gradient explosions. Furthermore,

  remains low (~9.3); TP/SL MAE flatlines at ~1,415–1,440 pips; `softmax_temp`

       `direction_weight=0.5` and `magnitude_weight=0.02` ($\delta=2.0$ Huber on
       NPUs), returning loss values to the clean $0.05\text{--}1.0$ numerical
       range.

       ($\min T = 0.75$), constrain Stress Protocol regularization ($\le 2.0$),

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_TRAINING_PATHOLOGY.md` (Nuclear Stability: AI Training Pathology Master Guide > 4. Modern 2026 Pathologies > Spatial Average Pooling Dilution (The Micro-Trigger Vanishing Defect) (Pathology 15)):

- **The Issue**: Standard Global Average Pooling ($\text{GAP}$) collapses a
  $H \times W \times C$ spatial activation tensor to $1 \times 1 \times C$ by
  averaging all spatial locations:

  $$
  \text{GAP}(x)_c = \frac{1}{H \cdot W} \sum_{h=1}^H \sum_{w=1}^W x_{c,h,w}
  $$

  For fine-grained tasks like micro-defect detection (compression blocking,
  localized noise, sensor blur) and safety filtering
  (`universal_nsfw_classification`), critical features occupy only
  $5\%\text{--}15\%$ of the image canvas. Averaging across the entire background
  dilutes the activation magnitude by $85\%\text{--}95\%$, preventing the
  classifier from learning decisive decision boundaries.

- **Identification**: High false negatives on localized micro-defects or small
  NSFW triggers; models require excessive global contrast to trigger
  classification responses.
- **Remedy**: **Spatial Statistical Pooling ($\text{Mean} \oplus \text{Std}$)**
  and **GeM Pooling**:

  $$
  \text{Feat}(x) = \left[ \text{GAP}(x) \,\|\, \text{StdDev}_{\text{spatial}}(x)
  \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{2C}
  $$

  $$
  \text{GeM}(x)_c = \left(\frac{1}{H \cdot W} \sum_{h,w}
  x_{c,h,w}^p\right)^{1/p}, \quad p \ge 3.0
  $$

  Statistical pooling preserves localized peak activation variance alongside
  scene-level context without adding convolutional FLOPs.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_TRAINING_PATHOLOGY.md` (Nuclear Stability: AI Training Pathology Master Guide > 5. High-Fidelity Strategy & Historical Evolution Taxonomy > The Max Stress LR Freeze (v16 Bug) (Pathology 55)):

**The Issue:** A logic gap in the Governor's `REFINEMENT` phase. When
`current_stress` reaches the maximum level of `5.0` and the model's quality
score is still far below `target_quality_score * 0.90`, the code falls through
to the `else` branch and applies `cooling_factor` (e.g., `0.85×`) to the LR
every single epoch. After 30–40 epochs at max stress, the LR is crushed to
near-zero, completely freezing the model's ability to escape the local minimum.
The stress plateau is permanent because the SOTA deactivation gate only fires
when quality *improves*, which is impossible with a frozen LR.

**Identification:** `metrics.csv` shows `Stress: 5.0` persisting for 20+ epochs.
PLCC/SRCC oscillate within a very narrow band (e.g., ±0.02). The LR column shows
exponential decay (e.g., `5e-5 → 2e-5 → 8e-6 → ...`). The terminal emits
`REFINEMENT: SOTA Precision Cooling` rather than any jolt message.

**Observed In:** `nima_aesthetic_mobile` run — 86 epochs, stress=5.0 from epoch
83+, PLCC stuck at 0.47 vs target 0.60, LR decaying from 5e-5 down toward the
`1e-5` absolute floor.

**Remedy:** **Max-Stress Jolt Guard (v16)**. Add a new `elif` branch in
`optimization_engine.py` between the stress-escalation block and the cooling
fallback. When `current_stress >= 5.0` and the model is still far from SOTA,
force the `jolt_multiplier` instead of the `cooling_factor`. Additionally, track
a `max_stress_stuck_epochs` counter. After `plateau_patience × 2` epochs in this
state with no improvement, emit a `[STUCK]` signal in the governor message so
the operator can make an informed decision about stopping or switching the
architecture backbone. This prevents indefinite silent degradation.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_TRAINING_PATHOLOGY.md` (Nuclear Stability: AI Training Pathology Master Guide > 4. Modern 2026 Pathologies > Turing Multi-GPU DataParallel Misalignment (The 16-byte Coalesce Fault) (Pathology 40)):

**The Issue:** When running PyTorch `DataParallel` on Turing-class GPUs (e.g.
Tesla T4), PyTorch packs all parameters into a single contiguous flat buffer to
broadcast them to replica GPUs (`_broadcast_coalesced`). If any parameter high
up in the model architecture has an odd size (e.g. an `out_channels=3` output
bias of exactly 3 floats / 12 bytes), it throws off the 16-byte memory alignment
boundary for *every single parameter* that follows it. While most operations
tolerate unaligned memory, heavily vectorized cuDNN algorithms (like `conv2d`
and `conv_transpose2d`) will immediately crash with a fatal
`CUDA error: misaligned address` or
`unable to find an engine to execute this computation`.

**Identification:** Model successfully trains on a single GPU but crashes with
`misaligned address` during the forward pass specifically on `replica 1` or
higher. Tracebacks point directly to standard cuDNN operations.

**Remedy:** **Global Alignment Monkey-Patch**. Do not alter the model's
`__init__` order (as this permanently corrupts the Optimizer state). Instead,
inject a global monkey-patch over `nn.Conv2d.forward` and
`nn.ConvTranspose2d.forward` that dynamically checks the raw memory pointer
(`weight.data_ptr() % 16`). If the pointer is unaligned (indicating a
DataParallel replica buffer), intercept the execution and force a `.clone()` to
instantly reallocate the tensor on PyTorch's native 256-byte aligned allocator
before passing it to `F.conv2d`.

Operational breakdown for `PAPER_TRAINING_SUITE.md` (LemGendary Model Training Suite: Technical Whitepaper > 7. Universal Instruction-Tuned Causal LLM Fine-Tuning & Dynamic Dataset Ingestion > 7.4. Multi-Turn ChatML Loss Formulation & Assistant-Only Prompt Masking):

During instruction tuning, computing loss across system prompts and user inputs
severely impairs model generalization by penalizing the model for memorizing
input tokens. The training engine enforces strict assistant-only supervised loss
masking:

1. **ChatML Serialization**: Formats multi-turn conversations into standard
   ChatML sequences:

   ```text
   system
   {system_prompt}
   user
   {user_message}
   assistant
   {assistant_response}
   ```

2. **Label Masking with -100 Ignored Index**: Token targets corresponding to
   system... and user... are
   assigned label -100. Only token targets within
   assistant... retain their token IDs:

   $$
   L_i = \begin{cases} -100 & \text{if token } i \in \text{Prompt (System/User)}
   \\ y_i & \text{if token } i \in \text{Assistant Response} \end{cases}
   $$

3. **CrossEntropy Loss & Perplexity Tracking**: PyTorch's
   `nn.CrossEntropyLoss(ignore_index=-100)` ignores masked prompt tokens during
   gradient backward passes. Real-time validation loss
   ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{CE}}$) is converted to validation Perplexity:

   $$
   \text{PPL} = \exp(\mathcal{L}_{\text{CE}})
   $$

convolutions under `torch.float16` autocast with batched tensors
($\text{batch\_size} \ge 2$, e.g. at $512\text{px}$). While single-sample
training passes ($\text{batch\_size} = 1$) compute cleanly, validation batches
produce immediate `NaN` values, cascading into $\text{ValLoss} = \text{NaN}$.

The hardware policy engine (`training/hardware/policy.py`) automatically detects
Turing non-Tensor-Core GPU architectures and forces full Float32 precision
(`amp_enabled = False`), permanently eliminating numerical corruption while
preserving full evaluation fidelity.

- **PyTorch Non-Writable Tensor Root Cause Remediation**: In
  `data/forex_dataset.py`, slicing into memory-mapped NumPy window arrays
  (`raw_sample = window[:, col_indices]`) yields non-contiguous, read-only
  memory views. In modern PyTorch 2.5+, passing non-writable NumPy arrays to
  `torch.from_numpy()` triggers an internal runtime `UserWarning` indicating
  undefined behavior if written to. Rather than suppressing the diagnostic with
  `warnings.filterwarnings` (strictly prohibited under LemGendary standards),
  the dataset layer introduces `_safe_from_numpy(arr)`:

  ```python
  def _safe_from_numpy(arr: np.ndarray) -> torch.Tensor:
      if not arr.flags.writeable:
          arr = arr.copy()
      return torch.from_numpy(arr)
  ```

  This creates an isolated, writable array buffer prior to tensor conversion,
  resolving PyTorch tensor instantiation at root cause with 0 runtime warnings
  and 0 tensor copying overhead during validation.
- **Telemetry Stream Segregation**: To prevent dense training iterations from
  degrading operator clarity, terminal output streams are segregated:
  1. High-frequency iteration steps stream as discrete, unconstrained percentage
     events.
  2. The Desktop GUI log feed (`LogPanel.tsx`, `TelemetryConsole.tsx`) filters
     intermediate batch updates to avoid terminal buffer churn, rendering
     discrete milestone notices (epoch start, validation completions, SOTA
     alerts, checkpoints).
  3. Visual progress is displayed via the dedicated `@radix-ui/react-progress`
     tracker component, maintaining peak visual ergonomics and zero stream
     interference.

`validate_one_epoch` (`training/training/validation.py`) computes FID with
`torchmetrics` `FrechetInceptionDistance(feature=2048)`, the 2048-dimensional
final pooling layer of Inception-v3, for every model with `fid` in
`sota_targets`. With real-image statistics $(\mu_r, \Sigma_r)$ and
reconstruction statistics $(\mu_g, \Sigma_g)$:

$$
\text{FID} = \lVert \mu_r - \mu_g \rVert_2^2 + \operatorname{Tr}\left(\Sigma_r +
\Sigma_g - 2 \left(\Sigma_r \Sigma_g\right)^{1/2}\right)
$$

Real and reconstructed `uint8` images are fed in micro-chunks of at most two
samples, so the transient Inception memory scales with the chunk, not with the
validation batch:

$$
\text{Mem}_{\text{peak}} = \mathcal{O}(b_{\text{chunk}} \cdot H \cdot W \cdot
C), \quad b_{\text{chunk}} \le 2
$$

- **Removed tool**: before v16.9.67, `tools/recalibrate_fid.py` rewrote
  `metrics.csv` FID values with formulas (for example `fid * 45 + lpips * 26`,
  and a fixed `2.78` for epoch 2) and recomputed `Quality_Score`. That broke the
  Chart & Metrics Governance and Publication-Grade FID rules, and the tool was
  removed.
- **Unverified FID history**: the rewritten rows of four models are not measured
  values: `codeformer`, `ffanet_indoor`, `mprnet_deraining` and
  `mirnet_lowlight`. Their historical FID values are **unverified** wherever

  no FID value for these models and publishes no replacement numbers.

- **Continuous Ranking Supervision**: Replaces non-differentiable sort
  operations with a continuous sigmoid-based soft ranking formulation:

  $$
  \tilde{r}_i^p = 1 + \sum_{j \ne i} \sigma\left(\frac{p_i - p_j}{\tau}\right),
  \quad \mathcal{L}_{\text{soft\_spearman}} = 1 - \frac{\text{Cov}(\tilde{r}^p,
  \tilde{r}^t)}{\sigma(\tilde{r}^p)\sigma(\tilde{r}^t)}
  $$

- **Micro-Batch Contrastive Memory Bank**: Employs a detached FIFO queue
  ($N=32/64$) to maintain historical representation context across gradient
  accumulation steps. On 4GB GPUs where physical micro-batch size is $b=2$, this
  scales active pair comparisons from $\binom{2}{2} = 1$ to
  $\binom{32}{2} = 496$ pairs per backward pass ($41.3\times$ rank gradient
  density) without increasing VRAM allocations.

- **VRAM Refit on Resolution Jumps**: after a jump the engine re-runs the
  VRAM audit at the new resolution (`training/training/batch_budget.py`) and
  fits the micro-batch to it; BatchNorm buffers and the train/eval mode are
  restored after the probe. The refit only shrinks the batch and runs only
  on CUDA. With an effective batch that has few divisors, the micro-batch
  can drop to 1.
- **Spatial Ladder Memory Analysis**: activation memory scales with the
  pixels held at once, so chunked evaluation bounds the peak by the chunk
  and not by the dataset size $N$. Along the restoration ladder
  `256px -> 384px -> 512px -> 640px`, $H \cdot W$ grows by 2.25, 1.78 and
  1.56 per step, 6.25 in total, so the micro-batch that fits at 256 px needs
  about $1/6.25$ of the memory budget per sample at 640 px. Under the
  exact-divisor rule an effective batch of 24 with a budget of 5 trains at
  4 x 6 and with a budget of 2 at 2 x 12.

According to `PAPER_TRAINING_SUITE.md` (LemGendary Model Training Suite: Technical Whitepaper > 2. High-Fidelity "Nuclear" Hardening > 2.19. Forex Parquet Locality & Telemetry Progress Sync (v16.9.26) (Part 1)):

- **Parquet Row-Group Locality Bottleneck & `RowGroupAwareSampler`**: Parquet is
  a columnar format organized into discrete row groups (typically ~5,000 rows
  each). Accessing row $N$ within a compressed row group requires decompressing
  the entire group. Under standard PyTorch `shuffle=True`, row indices are
  selected uniformly at random across all 700+ row groups across multiple years.
  This causes an catastrophic ~98% cache miss rate against in-memory LRU
  buffers, inflating batch iteration times to ~55 seconds per batch. The engine
  resolves this by integrating `RowGroupAwareSampler` directly in
  `training/core_loop.py` for all Forex datasets:
  1. Buckets sample indices by parent row group locality keys
     `('parquet', year, row_group_id)`.
  2. Shuffles at the row group level across epochs via
     `sampler.set_epoch(epoch)`.
  3. Yields indices within each row group contiguously, driving LRU cache hit
     rates from 2% to 99% and accelerating batch throughput to sub-second speeds
     (<0.5s/batch).

- **Continuous Ranking Supervision**: Replaces non-differentiable sort
  operations with a continuous sigmoid-based soft ranking formulation:

  $$
  \tilde{r}_i^p = 1 + \sum_{j \ne i} \sigma\left(\frac{p_i - p_j}{\tau}\right),
  \quad \mathcal{L}_{\text{soft\_spearman}} = 1 - \frac{\text{Cov}(\tilde{r}^p,
  \tilde{r}^t)}{\sigma(\tilde{r}^p)\sigma(\tilde{r}^t)}
  $$

- **Micro-Batch Contrastive Memory Bank**: Employs a detached FIFO queue
  ($N=32/64$) to maintain historical representation context across gradient
  accumulation steps. On 4GB GPUs where physical micro-batch size is $b=2$, this
  scales active pair comparisons from $\binom{2}{2} = 1$ to
  $\binom{32}{2} = 496$ pairs per backward pass ($41.3\times$ rank gradient
  density) without increasing VRAM allocations.

  `services/loose_pack_service.py`) packs a loose `images/` +

  stems, that every labelled sample has its JSON label and that the labels
  pass the shard verifier; only then dataset_info.yaml records `classes`

  index.json and the counts are resynced, and the loose folders are removed.
- Registry: `yolov8n` is `canonical_format: webdataset` (container primary
  webdataset), so the compiler and the modernize queue pack it as shards.

- `tests/unit/test_swa.py`: the SWA tests built a bare SGD optimizer and
  stepped `SWALR` with no optimizer step, so PyTorch warned that
  `lr_scheduler.step()` ran before `optimizer.step()` (`swa.py:92`). In a

  steps before `SwaPhase.end_epoch`, so production never hit it. A new

  was named `test_*`, so pytest collected it and warned that it returned
  a dict. It is now `run_multi_timeframe_live_pipeline`; the unittest
  wrapper still runs it and asserts on its outputs.
- The ONNX export keeps the TorchScript exporter (`dynamo=False`). The
  `torch.export` exporter passes the suite's export tests on tiny models,
  but nothing yet checks the exported graphs against onnxruntime for the
  real architectures and the FP16, onnxsim and WebGPU steps after it, so
  the switch is left to the owner. Its two DeprecationWarnings per export
  remain.

Operational breakdown for `README.md` (LemGendary Dataset Compiler Suite > Changelog > v16.9.52 - Seven Compiler Bugs Fixed; One Version String):

- **Compile CLI Configured**: `python -m core.manifold_compile` and
  `CompilerService` never installed their parsed arguments, so the workers
  raised from `get_args()` and `--workers`, `--image-format` and the
  strategy flags never reached `CONFIG`. `prepare_compile` now calls the new
  `compiler_config.install_args()`, and the pool initialiser receives the
  arguments.
- **Label Folders Created on Demand**: `write_label_file` creates
  `labels/`. Restoration, segmentation and diffusion manifolds with
  auto-labeling on used to lose every labelled sample because the folder
  did not exist.
- **Corrupt Parquet Shards**: an unreadable shard yields one `None` per row
  instead of records without a `name`, which raised `KeyError` in PASS 1.
  Nothing is registered, so the next run retries the shard.
- **MT5 Chunked Fallback**: the bar times are tz-aware UTC and the start
  date was naive, so the fallback always raised `TypeError`. The comparison
  now uses `dt_from` as a UTC timestamp.
- **Degrade Registry Commit**: `audit_events` (from `core.registry`) is keyed
  by `sample_id`; the degrade tool inserted a `sample_name`, so every
  non-dry-run failed at commit. The event now references the registry row.
  The tool also closes its SQLite connections.
- **Malformed `dataset_info.yaml`**: `/api/gui/datasets/with-stats` returned
  500 for a file that is not a mapping or not UTF-8. The new
  `read_yaml_mapping` and `as_count` helpers (also used by the datasets and
  Kaggle routes) log and ignore such files.
- **Module Entry Points**: package modules import `core`/`tools` absolutely
  and run only as `python -m pkg.module`. A test now fails if a launcher,
  route or document runs one by file path.
- **One Version String**: `core.cli_args.__version__` (API, `cli.py
  version`, `openapi.json`) was still 16.9.5. It now follows the README, and
  `tests/test_version_sync.py` keeps the three in step.
- Regression tests: `tests/test_known_bug_regressions.py`.

What are the operational constraints, verification steps, or key parameters for LemGendary Dataset Compiler Suite > Shard Label Format (JSON Only) in `README.md`?

Operational breakdown for `README.md` (LemGendary Dataset Compiler Suite > Shard Label Format (JSON Only)):

Inside WebDataset shards a sample's label is always `.json`; there are
no `.txt` label members. Masks stay `.mask.webp`. The schemas live in
one place, `utils/label_json.py` (module docstring and `LABEL_STRATEGIES`);
the strategy is the registry entry's `label_json`, else its task's
(`TASK_STRATEGIES`). Coordinates are normalised to 0..1, boxes are
`cx cy w h`.

- `face_landmarks` (detection-face, RetinaFace): `face_count`, `objects[]`
  with `category_id`, `bbox_cxcywh_normalized` and, when the face has real
  landmarks, `landmarks_normalized` (10 values). Labels rebuilt from source
  landmarks (`repair face-landmarks`) also record `landmark_source`.
- `yolo_boxes` (detection, pose, restoration, super-resolution,
  parameter_prediction): `object_count`, `objects[]` with `category_id`,
  `bbox_cxcywh_normalized` and, for pose lines, `keypoints`.
- `yolo_polygons` (segmentation): `object_count`, `objects[]` with
  `category_id`, `polygon_normalized`.
- `nima` (quality): `nima_scores` with `distribution` (10) and `mean_score`.
- `segmentation_mask` (face parsing, ParseNet): the class mask is the
  `.mask.webp` member (lossless, one class id per pixel); the JSON
  records `num_classes`, `class_names` and `mask_source`. A mask has no text
  label.
- `class_label` (classification): `class_id` (a number) or `class_name`.
  Labels written by `repair class-labels` carry both plus `label_source`;
  a pseudo label also `label_confidence` and `label_check_class`.
- `caption` (diffusion): `caption`.

An empty detection label is `{"object_count": 0, "objects": []}`: an image
without objects, kept as a valid negative. The shard verifier
